# Load packages

```{python}
from plotnine import * 
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
```

# Explore the dataset

Load data

```{python}
penguins = load_penguins()
```

First few rows of the dataste

```{python}
penguins.head()
```

Dimensions

```{python}
penguins.shape
```

Column names

```{python}
penguins.columns
```

# Graphics

```{python}
(ggplot( penguins, aes( x="bill_length_mm", y="bill_depth_mm" ) ) + geom_point() )
```

Colouring the points according to species types

```{python}
( ggplot(
        penguins,
        aes(
            x="bill_length_mm",
            y="bill_depth_mm",
            color="species"
        )
    )
    + geom_point()
)
```

Add labels

```{python}
( ggplot( penguins, aes( x="bill_length_mm", y="bill_depth_mm", color="species" ) ) + geom_point(size=3) + labs( title="Palmer Penguins", x="Bill length (mm)", y="Bill depth (mm)", color="Species" ) )
```

Add smooth trend

```{python}
( ggplot( penguins, aes( x="bill_length_mm", y="bill_depth_mm", color="species" ) ) + geom_point() + geom_smooth() + labs( title="Palmer Penguins", x="Bill length (mm)", y="Bill depth (mm)" ) )
```

# Note

You can also load the package as follows

```{python}
import plotnine as p9
```

Then, you have to use the prefix `p9`

```{python}
(p9.ggplot(penguins, p9.aes(x="bill_length_mm", y="bill_depth_mm", color="species" )) + p9.geom_point())
```
